title: Files, NIO, and resource management — Java Practice
description: Independent practice: The expense tracker exports and imports a local report. Seven questions with explanations.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: Why specify UTF-8 for an export?

options.text: To make text encoding explicit and interoperable

questions.explanation: Encoding determines how characters become bytes.

questions.prompt: Is split(",") a complete CSV parser?
questions.explanation: Quoted commas and multiline fields need proper CSV parsing.

questions.prompt: Which approach fits a file too large to fit comfortably in memory?

options.text: Convert it to a larger String

questions.prompt: Should untrusted native Java serialized objects be deserialized by default?
questions.explanation: Use a deliberately validated interchange format instead.

questions.prompt: A relative path is resolved against what?
questions.explanation: Process launch location affects relative paths.

questions.prompt: Does normalizing ../ segments alone defeat every path-traversal risk?

options.text: Only if the path is a String

questions.explanation: Symlinks and boundary checks require additional care.
A temporary path is allocated for this experiment. UTF-8 writes two records; the line stream counts 2. The stream closes before the temporary file is deleted.
